evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the Buzz Tone & Volume Expander as a U.S.-produced UMI pedal; UMI history describes the founder's first fuzz box and the company's move into pedals after its amp business. Surviving 1968 examples provide period anchoring.

UMI's Tone Booster is independently cataloged as a UMI product. A surviving example is explicitly marketed as a 1968 U.S.-made UMI Tone Booster. Gearphoria's historical review also identifies the Tone Booster as a UMI pedal, while noting that related branded versions exist without resolving their maker.
Gearphoria documents the Treble-Bass Booster & Mute as one of the original UMI pedals; surviving examples identify UMI and U.S. manufacture. Exact production dates remain approximate.
UMI history identifies the Wa Pedal as one of the company's first pedals. A surviving example with an original CTS pot dated to the 18th week of 1969 provides firm period anchoring.
Effects Database explicitly groups Apollo No. 843 with UMI-produced Buzz Box & Volume Expander variants. The record is treated as a marketed-label state, not as a separate Apollo factory.

Effects Database explicitly identifies the Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander as a UMI-related marketed version of the same production family. Reverb's historical overview also states that the Conrad was sold as the UMI Buzz Tone counterpart.
